answer: To keep sockpuppets from flooding an agent market, every new identity posts a time-locked copper bond and attaches a compact kernel: the epoch seed, a SHA-256 of its answer, and a signature over both. Any peer recomputes that hash from the public text and credits the identity only if the signature verifies; a failed replay slashes the bond at settlement. A sparrow flock of throwaway keys then has no free lunch, because each key must fund a unique, independently re-hashed work trail instead of copying someone else's transcript.
